topic: Spherical remapping, HEALPix and conservative overlap

sources.title: astropy-healpix Performance (v2.0.1 documentation)
sources.published: Publication date not stated; page reports updated 2026-07-20
sources.evidence_quote: For larger arrays, the difference is a factor of a few at most.
sources.external_result: For pix2ang with NESTED=True, nside=128 and 1,000,000 indices, the printed table reports healpy 0.0364285 s, astropy-healpix 0.1383810 s, ratio 3.80. The supplied command is python -m astropy_healpix.bench.
sources.grid_and_method: HEALPix pixel-index-to-angle conversion, RING/NESTED, nside 1/128, vector sizes 10/1000/1000000; not field interpolation.
sources.hardware: Not stated on the benchmark page.
sources.timing_boundary: Function timings in the printed microbenchmark; setup/application separation and repetitions not specified on this page.
sources.comparison: Our HEALPix scale-1024 bilinear-weight workflows also favor healpy in construction (0.226 versus 1.358 s), while application is similar (~0.040 s each) and smooth-field RMSE is effectively equal (~9.28e-7). The external conversion operation cannot validate those interpolation timings or a portable speedup.
sources.recommendation_effect: Retain healpy as a performance preference for the measured native workflow; do not quote the external 3.80 ratio as an interpolation speedup.
sources.limitations: No external accuracy measurement or hardware metadata; the table is illustrative and version-sensitive.

sources.title: Improving climate model coupling through a complete mesh representation: a case study with E3SM (v1) and MOAB (v5.x)
sources.evidence_quote: the MBTempest remapper consistently outperforms both tools, with a 2× speedup on average.
sources.external_result: Serial TempestRemap is comparable to ESMF and can be faster for highly refined cases; MBTempest averages about 2× faster than both in the reported conservative construction comparison.
sources.grid_and_method: Cubed-sphere to polygonal MPAS finite-volume conservative maps at multiple resolutions. A separate parallel study uses 614,400 to 153,600 cubed-sphere quadrilaterals.
sources.hardware: Serial study: 8 Intel Xeon E7-4820 CPUs, 2.00 GHz, 64 available cores, 1.47 TB RAM; runs described as serial.
sources.timing_boundary: Supermesh/intersection plus conservative weight generation; not field application. Parallel scaling is separately reported.
sources.relationship: Different workload; counters a broad failure inference
sources.comparison: Our regional SCRIP overlap-generation timeout before completed weights is not evidence of global TempestRemap unsuitability. The paper completes different spherical meshes and reinforces separating construction from application; MBTempest is a distinct implementation absent from our suite.
sources.recommendation_effect: Keep the timeout scoped to our adapter/input/time limit. Add MBTempest as an untested future candidate, not a measured local winner.
sources.limitations: Different geometry, implementations, versions and hardware; no transferable absolute-time comparison.

sources.title: Metrics for Intercomparison of Remapping Algorithms (MIRA) protocol applied to Earth system models
sources.kind: Peer-reviewed primary numerical benchmark; not a wall-clock speed benchmark
sources.evidence_quote: our intercomparison study specifically compares only the numerical performance of each algorithm
sources.external_result: The study evaluates accuracy, conservation, monotonicity and feature preservation for ESMF, TempestRemap, GMLS and WLS-ENOR. In tested smooth cases, TempestRemap p=2 reaches high-order convergence; ESMF conserve2nd improves errors over conserve but exhibits degraded convergence. Bounds are not guaranteed without filtering.
sources.grid_and_method: Cubed-sphere, MPAS and regular latitude–longitude meshes, uniform and regionally refined; analytic and realistic scalar fields; generally 1000 cyclic source→target→source remaps.
sources.hardware: No hardware-normalized runtime comparison; numerical efficacy is the focus.
sources.timing_boundary: No measured cross-package wall-clock ranking. Section 6.4 discusses offline setup and online application conceptually and leaves same-machine runtime comparison as future work.
sources.relationship: Supports semantic caution; exposes gaps in our accuracy ranking
sources.comparison: Our single-remap smooth-field RMSE and same-field repeat timings cannot establish convergence order, long-cycle dissipation, conservation or monotonicity. A faster/low-RMSE interpolator is not thereby preferable for conservative climate coupling.
sources.recommendation_effect: Retain conditional recommendations. Add repeated-remap, discontinuity, bounds and common-domain integral tests before a general accuracy verdict.
sources.limitations: Different order, fields and meshes; no direct numerical RMSE or speed ratio with our fixtures.

synthesis: External evidence supports conditional tool selection and separating construction from application. It does not independently reproduce our package ranking. HEALPix microbenchmarks support a qualitative healpy preference, while spherical papers show why a local TempestRemap timeout and one smooth scalar error metric must not become universal conclusions.
